title: dream comes true
author: Glittering_Lime_4777
selftext: personally, i think the best part of ai game dev is not for making commercial games that puts millions into your bank account, but watching the dream game in your brain finally comes true, I always imagine a cute little pistol clearing floors of enemies using his own recoil, but I can never make my imagination come to life due to how frustrating it is for me to code, with ai, I can finally see the pistol shooting blobs and cutely ascend to the next floor which without ai, it takes much more efforts to learn and achieve. I hope people give less hate to ai and appreciate how it can visualize our creative ideas with ease

replies.author: BattlersNetwork
replies.body:
I can see how that would make sense to people. As for checking out, I do not owe you any argument or explanations, unfortunately.
 I merely wanted to suggest that you possibly do not have all the information to make a sound judgement. After that, it is your choice to do with that info what you will. You have made your choice clear. Cheers.

replies.author: snezna_kraljica
replies.body:
\>  As for checking out, I do not owe you any argument or explanations, unfortunately.

Of course not, but this is a forum for communication not a shoutbox. I was hoping for a bit of human interaction and exchange of view to learn an grow. alas... 

\> I merely wanted to suggest that you possibly do not have all the information to make a sound judgement. 

I can go from what there is. I understand something different under "gatekeeping". I asked for clarification as it does not make sense to me and I gave a few examples.

Instead of getting an explanation who I am wrong I got hit with "you're wrong, bye". That's not helpful, neither do I understand the goal of such an interaction.

replies.author: BattlersNetwork
replies.body:
I like this reply better. The others made me assume you might have been closed-minded and I am not fond of preaching to deaf ears. 

Time is a currency, friend. Time must be spent to learn a new skill, to refine the skill, and to apply the skill. Coding itself, nevermind making a whole game, is very expensive time wise. 

Unfortunately, those experiencing poverty need to expend more of their Time just to live. That means spending extra Time for extra hours at work and for multiple jobs. Spending extra Time trying to find the cheapest groceries, or one's self or dependants go hungry. Spending extra time on the phone trying to get bills reduced, payment dates extended, or looking for any sort of benefits at all. Spending Time dealing with the mental disorders which may manifest from experiencing these stresses. 

This isnt even close to a quarter of what poverty does to an individual, and we are only speaking of Time being gatekept here. 

The availablity of technology is not a sound argument either, friend. How can anyone with a smartphone and access to AI be handicapped from learning a skill in any way? Well I can personally take a houseless person about a block and a half from my place to a little yellow tent where they will be assigned a smartphone from the government with the capabilities to handle ChatGPT. And I am going to assume you would not be asking this same houseless person 'What is stopping you from learning to code if you have the luxuries of a smartphone and AI?'. This is an extreme case, yes, but the point stands. The access to technology is no longer a status symbol which represents freedom of time and choice as it did in the past.

So yes, despite what anyone believes, poverty gatekeeps individuals in one of the worse ways imaginable on this planet. And I will double down and call you and all those who are unaware of its effects blessed.

replies.author: snezna_kraljica
replies.body:
I understand poverty (even though I just experienced it probably in a very light European kind of way). I understand time being limited, I understand pressure and stress.

Time of AI dev spend for oneself as OP is a bad investment as a poor person. You'd be better of learning a skill than doing that. Also free.

I'm also not arguing that being poor comes with limitations.

But those are not gatekeeping. That's just wrong terminology and creates a victim mindset about "others are preventing me from doing that" instead of "I must do better to afford X".

It's a different thing if I can't have a thing or if somebody is actively preventing me from reaching a state where I can have X. Not being able to code because I'm not admitted to university because of my heritage = gatekeeping. Being not smart enough to get education != gatekeeping. 

It's colloquially used if somebody doesn't give you what is freely available, like information. This is not the case here. Everybody has the same amount of time.

replies.author: BattlersNetwork
replies.body:
You seem to not understand how much external factors effect whether one has the capacity to "pull themselves out" of a bad situation. I do not understand European societal classes, but if your understanding of them limits you from seeing poverty as a gatekeeper, then perhaps European poverty is not as bad as American poverty, though I don't very much believe this. And with that we are back to me hoping you are grateful to not know what you don't know. The best you can do is trust that it gets worse than you personally believe, and to have some sympathy for those who might be experiencing it. 

I avoided speaking of my own experiences to remain objective, but I assure you I have personally lived through enough of what I speak of. 

"Everybody has the same amount of time." I just explained to you how Time = Money especially when experiencing poverty. Go ahead and substitute those two words and see if that still hits the same, friend.

I wish we could have had a better setting to talk and more time, but here and now are neither of those.

Cheers.

replies.author: snezna_kraljica
replies.body:
I think we're talking past each other. I'm not saying poverty is not bad and is a structural issue society needs to solve. I agree.

I disagree in this context of OP building AI calling "knowledge" a gatekeeper because you need to learn before you can do and make an effort. This is a dangerous mindset to go forward calling putting in the work "gatekeeping". 

It's two different things.

replies.author: w1zinvestmentss
replies.body: This makes no sense. We are talking about building software. I have created professional grade databases that thousands of people use. Years ago, it took a ton of manual work. Now, the barrier of entry is lowered, and more people can create databases. Instead of crying about it, it's on me to utilize AI to make new cool things faster. I can now use my professional expertise to add taste. Back then certain tools were quite expensive, i.e. tableau, now people can create their own things with less money. The same for coding, I am not a coder, and have built a functional web app with the help of AI. There was a level of arrogance from some programers, and artists (i.e. I am too good to work with you and financial barriers) In some cases you needed an enterprise licence to build, your average joe can't afford that. AI is taking over, and people like me and others are going to use our passion and creativity to make cool shit that helps people.

replies.author: snezna_kraljica
replies.body:
Who is crying about AI? I use it heavily everyday professionally.

I'm complaining about people saying "having to acquire knowledge and skill for a thing" is gatekeeping. That's a very weird usage of that word which is used to say someone is preventing me from accessing otherwise free information. Not that I'm gatekept by own incompetence.

"Especially the ones who are passionate about something, no more gatekeepers or begging others to build your vision. "

Who was keeping you before from fulfilling your vision?

\> e. Back then certain tools were quite expensive, i.e. tableau, now people can create their own things with less money

Knowledge hasn't been expensive since the days of Google.

\> The same for coding, I am not a coder, and have built a functional web app with the help of AI.

So? Who was keeping you beforehand from learning it from free courses and resources all over the world?

\> ) In some cases you needed an enterprise licence to build,

Which one?

\> AI is taking over, and people like me and others are going to use our passion and creativity to make cool shit that helps people.

Cool. Never had a problem with that. I have just a "problem" (if one might call it that) in the mindest of those people that some evil force was preventing them beforehand doing it.  Lets be real for second, it was the necessary effort, work and time which needed to be put in which prevented you.

Similar as I'm gatekept from having an athletic body because I need to go and workout in the gym. Rightfully so everybody would say pushups and running is free, you need to put the work in.

replies.author: w1zinvestmentss
replies.body:
Those are fair points, I wish you all the best and agree to disagree. I too believe that hard work is necessary, I grind hard professionally and play a ton of sports. With that said, not everything can be done on your own, and there is and was a degree of gatekeeping happening among artists and coders, which has been alleviated by AI. If you disagree, I expect to see you build your own version of GTA 6 in a couple of years, as all you have to do is grind. Or whatever is the highest level of technology in your field. I have a more of nuanced view, and understand that things are in our control, but more people will have a new avenue to create in some aspects thanks to AI. I'm guilty of this myself, I'm sure I could have learned how to code earlier, but having AI as a teacher has been amazing. If I was to ask coders to teach me for free like AI has, I'm sure they would rightfully say no.
Have a great day.

replies.author: snezna_kraljica
replies.body:
\> and there is and was a degree of gatekeeping happening among artists and coders, which has been alleviated by AI.

Which is why I originally inquired about. What was gatekept? I honestly interested. When I was a aspiring dev I was so happy about all the free only resources and communities sharing their wisdom and engaging in how to do things. Same as an artist, so many tipps and tricks and support to keep pushing and exercising and learning.

I'm really honestly confused about how one could think any different. Because those people won't work for free to create your vision? Since when are you entitled to anybodys time. Each and every individual has their own idea.

\> If you disagree, I expect to see you build your own version of GTA 6 in a couple of years, as all you have to do is grind.

I didn't say that. But I'm also not saying I'm gatekept from doing GTA6. Some things take more effort and knowledge or resources I have. That doesn't make it gatekeeping.

As in my example, I'm not gatekept from having a Ferrari.

\> If I was to ask coders to teach me for free like AI has, I'm sure they would rightfully say no. 

You're wrong here. There's tons of free info and communities on the net to teach you. Heck that's how I've learned and that was back in the 90s.

replies.author: w1zinvestmentss
replies.body:
Seems like we agree on some things which is great.
You seem fixated on the word gatekeeping. Read other comments, talking about money. As a direct response to your questions about artists; I want artists to get paid, and I'm happy to see them win. It sounds like you haven't studied art closely or the behind the scenes. A direct example: I love the music producer Mike Dean who has worked with Travis Scott, the weekend, etc. Regardless of money, Mike Dean may not want to ever work with me as I am a nobody. Even if I offer him his typical wage. And he's not wrong for that. There is a circle of elite artists who they don't care about money, they are not working with little guys unless it is a favour. And they should have that artistic right. Thus, the ability to work with great producers you like and use their connections is gate kept. Now, with music software, I can work with producers on their level (with the properly decentralize licensing)
This is a direct example that no matter how much I love these producers, their circle can chose to blackball me, exclude me etc. This is a well known complaint from smaller artists. This happens around many  industries. If you think we are living in this perfect world where you can always get what you want, you are wrong in that area in my opinion. Sounds like we both agree hard work and learning is necessary. I disagree with the way you are downplaying gatekeeping that has been reported by many; if you want to diminish their experience and prespectives, that is your choice lol

replies.author: snezna_kraljica
replies.body:
\>You seem fixated on the word gatekeeping.   
  
Sure I am, that's my whole question since my first comment in this thread.

The situation you describe with big stars is also not gatekeeping. It's their prerogative what they do with their time. They are not keeping you from you doing your own thing though. 

\> If you think we are living in this perfect world where you can always get what you want, you are wrong in that area in my opinion.

Where did I state that? I've said explicitly that you not being able to have everything is not gatekeeping, that's all. 

Gatekeeping is e.g. you want to learn about something or join a group and you're not allowed or something which doesn't cost somebody anything and they have no damage from it (like sharing info/knowledge) is not shared. 

Words have meaning and suggesting that developers or artists are preventing you from finding your own success because you are not entitled to their time is delusional. That's not gatekeeping.

replies.author: w1zinvestmentss
replies.body:
You gave a poor response to the music example. Have a great day and wish to the best. You don't understand how industries work lol 
I never once said I'm entitled to anything, my point is if you want to work with the top people in the industry, they can choose not work with you. Hence you do not have access to resources. In addition, before you needed access to artists, composers, coders, animators. 

Prove to me that you have done this on your own and think it's doable for your average person. I speak in population averages not one offs. 

Good luck with everything, you have failed to provide a proper arguement.

replies.author: snezna_kraljica
replies.body:
Stop gatekeeping me from a discussion.

That's poor from you, why engage in a discussion and leave with a poor excuse like the other guy "no you're wrong, bye". This is a place for discussion and exchange for everybody to grow.

\>  my point is if you want to work with the top people in the industry, they can choose not work with you. 

Sure and that's not called gatekeeping.

replies.author: w1zinvestmentss
replies.body: Thank you. I make okay money now, but my heart goes out to those struggling.l financially. When you are struggling to survive, it's hard to sit down and learn how to code. Now, if you have an idea, the barrier to create software is lowered. It still takes a ton of work, but it is possible to build on your own. I remember trying to hire people years ago and some people would quote very high numbers (rightfully so) now I'm sure they are open to work. Also, some artists refuse to work with some people, that is a form of gatekeeping.

comments.author: snezna_kraljica
comments.body: Creative ideas come from restriction and learning. It's a fundamental part of it. Iconic characters like Mario stem from the fact that there just was a 16x16px grid and you had to think really hard and try so much stuff until you got it right. If AI is in just solving all your ideas directly I think you're missing out a lot of the good stuff that comes from learning and a challenge.

replies.author: w1zinvestmentss
replies.body: This is a fair point. I think the key will come from testing and iteration, but I can see how alot of great games were built from the manual grind.
